|strategy=By [mailto:strwars@aol.com Royce Russell], Gold 15<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20020619222407/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/garindan.html</ref>

If you are the type of player who likes to surprise your opponent then take another look at [[Garindan]]. His modest deploy cost makes him a welcome addition to any deck. He is one of my favorite aliens to play. He has a high destiny number, which comes in handy when playing against a numbers deck, and he is also a spy! His real strength comes from his game text. When with a Rebel such as [[Owen Lars]], or any of the Rebels with ability greater than 2, your Imperials deploy -1 there! Hey, any amount of Force that you can shave off deployment costs is worth a lot in surprise value. Plus, say you need to send in backups to [[Garindan]]'s site, no problem, if that pesky Rebel of high ability is still present, your Imperials at adjacent sites can move to [[Garindan]]'s site for free!

Combos:

[[Garindan]] + [[Hoth]]:Mountains + Lots of 2 deploy Imperials.

This could be a fun combo in a [[Hoth]] deck. Lure a Rebel of ability greater than 2 to your location and then deploy all the Imperials in your hand for next to nothing. Lure [[Luke Skywalker]] to the [[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Mountains]] (Light Side gets a +1 Force drain so this should be easy), then deploy [[Garindan]], [[DS-61-2]], [[DS-61-3]], and [[DS-61-4]] for just a mere 2 Force, and have a power of 8 and plenty of ability! You could even add [[General Veers]] for just one more Force for a total power of 11! With a deploy -2 the possibilities are endless.

[[Garindan]] + [[Undercover]].

Use this simple combo to block your opponents Force drain. Plus, you still get the -1 deploy for your Imperials if there is a Rebel with ability greater than 2 at the same location. This is a way to gain a slight advantage over an entrenched Rebel force. Let the games begin!
